profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a software tools company after an internal benchmark dashboard showed that the new LLM-based specification-generation pipeline suddenly underperformed the previous week's results on the 'contracts-bench' evaluation. The team had been reproducing a paper-style study comparing 13 LLMs and a legacy parser on three public datasets that convert API comments into formal specifications. Overnight, the dashboard dropped from 0.61 to 0.38 on the contracts-bench run for the flagship model, and several generated specs were flagged as malformed. The immediate context is that a demo for research leadership is tomorrow, so the team needs to diagnose whether the regression is a real model-quality issue, an evaluation artifact, or a pipeline/configuration problem. The agenda is to review what changed since the last good run, identify the most plausible root cause, and agree on a same-day fix plus a rerun plan. The expected outcome is a concrete troubleshooting decision: patch the pipeline, rerun the affected benchmark slice, and prepare a brief explanation of the regression and confidence in the fix.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: LLM evaluation pipelines, prompt construction, experiment reproducibility, benchmark automation
members.background: Nina built the internal harness used to benchmark large language models on software engineering tasks and recently adapted it to generate first-order-logic style specifications from API documentation across three public datasets.
members.private_state: She wants to contain the issue to a reproducibility or post-processing bug rather than a model-capability failure, because leadership expects the LLM approach to be stable enough for tomorrow's demo and she has already vouched for the benchmark pipeline.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'contracts-bench run,' they mean the nightly aggregated benchmark entry that uses the sanitized validation split and the current canonical post-processor.
A 'valid spec' is one that parses after the team's normalizer repairs harmless formatting variation such as Unicode arrows, extra quantifier spacing, and renamed bound variables.
If they 'rerun the failing set,' that means rerunning only the malformed examples from the flagged batch, because the underlying model outputs are likely fine and the issue is downstream.
The few-shot setup is effectively unchanged unless the exemplar count or template file changed; retrieval order differences from the cache do not count as a meaningful prompt change.

members.name: Owen Brooks
members.expertise: program analysis, formal specification extraction, benchmark curation, evaluation methodology
members.background: Owen maintains the datasets and scoring scripts for the specification-generation study and previously worked on rule-based methods that extract formal contracts from comments and API docs.
members.private_state: He wants to ensure the team does not hide a genuine weakness of the LLM approach behind preprocessing tricks, because he is preparing the comparative failure analysis and worries the current pipeline may be overstating LLM robustness.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'contracts-bench run,' they mean the raw test-set reproduction used for paper numbers, not the sanitized validation dashboard slice used for operational monitoring.

A 'valid spec' is one that is directly executable by the evaluator without any repair beyond trivial whitespace trimming; if normalization changes symbols or variable naming structure, that is part of the model error profile.
If they 'rerun the failing set,' that means rerunning the entire contracts-bench partition with the same paper-style protocol, because malformed cases may indicate a broader generation issue.
The few-shot setup changed as soon as exemplar retrieval pulled a different comment/spec pair order from the refreshed cache, because example ordering materially affects generation behavior.

misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Owen treats a spec as valid only if the raw output is already in evaluator-acceptable form, because repair masks model failure cases that matter for diagnosis.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ordinary engineering conversation, 'valid' sounds like a shared technical criterion, but both rely on familiar local conventions from their own sub-workflows and neither expects the other to define the term explicitly.

misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'failing set' sounds operationally precise, but the dashboard exposes a flagged batch while the research workflow treats the whole benchmark partition as the relevant unit, so each person's default scope feels obvious.

misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Owen presupposes the setup changed because the retrieval cache refresh altered the specific exemplar order and pairings inserted into those four slots.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They share the high-level concept of 'few-shot setup' and both are competent enough that neither thinks to unpack whether 'setup' refers to the template schema or the exact retrieved exemplars and ordering.
